items.title: PM Anwar: China visit yields RM28b in potential investments across high‑tech sectors
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Malaysia has secured more than RM28 billion in potential investments following trade talks with major Chinese industry players, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The high-impact investments span several strategic sectors, including semiconductor manufacturing, artificial intelligence, robotics, electric vehicles, biotechnology, and advanced medical devices. “Overall, these business meetings recorded potential investments valued at over RM28 billion,” said Anwar.

items.title: Air quality dips in Sarawak with nine areas unhealthy, Melaka also affected
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — A total of nine areas in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 4pm today, with the Serian District Police Headquarters (IPD) recording the highest reading at 200. Meanwhile, 48 areas recorded moderate readings, including Batu Muda, Kuala Lumpur (75); Keningau, Sabah (60); Seberang Perai, Penang (53); and Kota Bharu, Kelantan (52). Another 11 areas recorded good readings.

items.title: RTM to air Harimau Malaya matches live, PM urges Malaysians to show support
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM) will broadcast Malaysia's matches in the FIFA Asean Cup 2026 live, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar said the decision followed questions from the public on social media yesterday about whether the national team's matches would be shown live. he said.

items.title: 40kph limit introduced at Federal Highway motorcycle crash site, lane resurfaced
items.summary: Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the improvements would be carried out following initial action by the Public Works Department (PWD) at the site. "Following this, improvement works, including milling and paving the road surface and installing a 40kph advisory speed sign, will be carried out," he said in a Facebook post today. Nanta said preliminary information showed that the coloured surface on the motorcycle lane had been designed and applied as an anti-skid treatment in accordance with the specified work requirements.

items.title: Emrail loses RM59m LRT3 bond suit, ordered to pay Kuwait Finance House RM39m
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — In a double courtroom defeat for rail contractor Emrail Sdn Bhd, the High Court has dismissed its RM59.1 million lawsuit against Kuwait Finance House (M) Bhd (KFH) and ordered the company alongside three personal guarantors to pay the bank RM39.09 million. Justice Quay Chew Soon dismissed Emrail's claim over a disputed performance bond for the Light Rail Transit 3 (LRT3) development in its entirety and allowed KFH’s counterclaim in full, holding the contractor and its guarantors jointly and severally liable for the outstanding debt, FMT reported. The court further established that the specific performance bond template required by Emrail was never incorporated into the financing agreement with KFH.

items.title: Digital assets already contributing to economic activity, but potential remained uncertain
items.summary: SC digital strategy and innovation executive director Dr Wong Huey Ching said digital assets were already contributing to economic activity, although their longer-term potential remained uncertain. She said the presence of companies and firms operating in Malaysia and employing people in the digital asset space was encouraging from an economic growth perspective. Wong said SC saw potential for digital assets and blockchain-based solutions to address issues in the capital market.

items.title: Indonesia court reduces Gojek founder's sentence to 9 years in appeal hearing
items.summary: JAKARTA: An Indonesian court has reduced the prison sentence of Gojek founder and former education minister Nadiem Makarim to 9 years from 10 years in an appeal hearing for a graft conviction relating to improper laptop procurement, judges said on Thursday. He filed an appeal on July 1 to the Jakarta high court. The court also cut the amount of restitution Nadiem must pay from 809 billion rupiah ($45.23 million) to 548 billion rupiah, another judge, Subachran Hardi Mulyana, said.

items.title: Media Prima hosts PNB delegation at Balai Berita
items.summary: The delegation, led by PNB president and group chief executive Datuk Rizal Rickman Ramli, was received by Media Prima Bhd group managing director Datuk Rafiq Razali at Anjung Liku, Balai Berita Bangsar. The visit included tours of Media Prima Bhd facilities, including Media Prima Audio, News and Current Affairs and Wanita Hari Ini (WHI) Studio, Rev Media Group and the KLIK editorial floor. Among those present were Media Prima Content and TV Networks and Primeworks Studios chief executive officer Nini Yusof, Media Prima Audio chief executive officer Nazri Noran, and Media Prima News and Current Affairs Division group managing editor Jasbant Singh.

items.title: Couple acquitted of trafficking 81.77g methamphetamine in Kelantan
items.summary: Judicial Commissioner Azhar Mokhtar made the ruling after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against Syed Mohamad Haizat Syed Hassan, 32, and Nurul Syahira Zakaria, 30, at the end of the prosecution's case. He said the accused's house could also be accessed by anyone through the main entrance or the kitchen. "Next to the accused's house is a car wash where three workers often used the toilet at the house.

items.title: MCMC backs police crackdown as Op Pedo nets 53 suspects, eight of them teens
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 24 — The collaboration between the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) continues to be strengthened to combat the misuse of network services for the purpose of online child sexual exploitation. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MCMC, as the technical agency, would continue to play an important role in assisting PDRM, especially the D11 Division (Sexual, Women and Child Investigation) of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), in tracking down those who misuse network services and subsequently bringing them to justice. Fahmi said the collaboration also involved technical and forensic aspects to assist PDRM investigations into online child sexual exploitation activities.

items.title: Pas hits out at Penang Umno's push to strengthen PH-BN ties
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang Pas has hit out at state Umno's push to strengthen ties with Pakatan Harapan, saying the move puts political cooperation ahead of Malay-Muslim unity. Penang Pas information chief Ustaz Muhammad Fawwaz Mohamad Jan said unity should remain the primary agenda for Malay-Muslims at both state and national levels. He criticised state Umno leader Datuk Rashidi Zinol for advocating closer cooperation with PH despite DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng publicly calling for Umno's removal from the state administration.

items.title: Sabah sees 10 million searches on Xiaohongshu as China tourism interest surges
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 24 — Sabah has recorded over 10 million searches on REDnote (Xiaohongshu), China’s leading social and lifestyle platform, signalling a massive surge in interest from Chinese travellers, said Datuk Jafry Ariffin The Sabah minister of tourism, culture and environment disclosed the figures following his visit to the REDnote office in Shanghai yesterday, noting that the high search volume underscores Sabah’s strong visibility in the Chinese market. “This is a very encouraging indication for Sabah. “China remains an important tourism market for Sabah.

items.title: Nominee intervention halts consent judgment in Zetrix AI dividend dispute
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ongoing legal tangle over the dividend payout of Zetrix AI Bhd has escalated, with the two nominees of an unnamed substantial shareholder being officially granted permission by the High Court to intervene in a lawsuit between the substantial shareholder and the company's share registrar. Zetrix AI announced the intervention today, which caused a proposed consent judgment directed by its board to the Share Registrar of the company to enter with the substantial shareholder be halted. The latest development of the legal case has resulted in a computation mismatch in the designated dividend accounts, resulting in computation delays by the company in the remittance of the dividend payment to shareholders, said Zetrix AI.

items.title: Smart seeks Budget 2027 boost to keep rescue gear ahead of the curve
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Continued investment in the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) is necessary to ensure it remains equipped with the latest search and rescue technology and equipment, says National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim. He said Nadma hoped its allocation request under Budget 2027 would be approved to allow SMART to acquire new equipment in line with developments in search and rescue operations. "Just like the handphones we use today, technology and equipment for search and rescue operations are constantly evolving, requiring Smart to keep pace," he said at a press conference after the closing ceremony of Smart's International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (Insaraq) Heavy Urban Search and Rescue (Heavy Usar) recertification programme.

items.title: Family planning knowledge in the country remains low
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Knowledge of family planning methods among Malaysians remains low, with only 34 per cent of married couples using modern contraceptives. The findings of the Study on Family Planning Practices in Malaysia also showed that misconceptions about contraceptive use had led some couples to be reluctant to use them. National Population and Family Development Board chairman Datuk Seri Rohani Abdul Karim said the findings highlighted the need to strengthen literacy, access to and use of family planning services so that couples could make informed decisions regarding pregnancy based on their family's needs and financial capabilities.

items.title: Police announce staged KL diversions as Sunday Coway Run shuts 34 roads
items.summary: “The roads involved are Jalan Stadium, Jalan Maharajalela, Jalan Dewan Bahasa, Jalan Bukit Petaling, Jalan Bellamy, Jalan Hang Tuah, Jalan Hang Jebat, Jalan Sultan Ismail, Jalan Raja Chulan, Jalan Conlay and Jalan Kia Peng. “Also involved are Jalan Perak, Jalan P. Ramlee, Jalan Ampang, Jalan Raja Laut, Jalan Putra, Jalan Tun Ismail, Jalan Tunku, Jalan Langgak Tunku, Jalan Pinggiran Tunku, Jalan Girdle, Jalan Bukit Tunku and Jalan Sultan Salahuddin,” he said in a statement today. He said that other roads that would also be closed were Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar, Jalan Persiaran Sultan Salahuddin, Jalan Parlimen, Jalan Dato Onn, Bulatan Dato Onn, Jalan Kinabalu, Jalan Tun Perak, Jalan Pudu, Jalan Sultan, Jalan Petaling and Bulatan Merdeka.

items.title: Masidi confident Putrajaya will secure Sabah borders amid Balabac Strait concerns
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 24 — Sabah Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun is confident the federal government will safeguard the state's borders in the Balabac Strait, despite concerns surrounding a US-backed Philippine military facility in the region. Speaking to reporters after the Sabah Carbon Forum today, Masidi said that border security falls under the jurisdiction of Putrajaya. When asked if Sabah would see additional security reinforcements, Masidi replied, “All I can say is that I don’t think they will allow Sabah to go undefended.”

items.title: Man claims trial over alleged attack on 79-year-old aunt
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An unemployed man today pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court to voluntarily causing grievous hurt to his 79-year-old aunt. Kok entered his plea before Judge Noor Aini Yusof. Deputy public prosecutor Mohamad Fadhly Mohd Zamry sought RM20,000 bail and conditions requiring Kok to refrain from harassing prosecution witnesses and surrender his passport until the case is disposed of.

items.title: Father, teenage son held over Kuala Kangsar murder of woman with disabilities
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 24 — A father and son have been remanded for seven and two days respectively, starting today, to assist in the investigation of a murder case involving a woman with disabilities (PwD) in Kampung Cheh Kati, Kuala Kangsar, yesterday. Kuala Kangsar district police chief ACP Heisham Harun said the police received a report regarding the incident at 2.38pm after family members discovered the victim lying face down and unconscious. A woman was found dead in the living room of a house in Kampung Cheh Kati, Kuala Kangsar on September 23, 2026.

items.title: Ismail calls for review of directive barring state exco from offices
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has called for authorities to review the order barring state executive councillors (exco) from entering their offices at Wisma Negeri. "I was informed that there was a restriction or directive barring exco members from entering their respective offices. KW Negri Sembilan, state, Ismail Lasim, © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Sarawak's 17 new state seats unlikely to make next election — EC
items.summary: KUCHING: The 17 proposed new Sarawak state seats are unlikely to be in place for the next state election, Election Commission (EC) chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said. He said the review of the electoral boundaries for the seats would take longer than February 2027, when the term of the Sarawak government expires. In July, the Sarawak Legislative Assembly passed the State Legislative Assembly (Composition of Members) Bill 2025 to add 17 new seats, bringing the total number of seats from 82 to 99.

items.title: ‘Income first’: Economy Minister Akmal says Budget 2027 must deliver better wages for Malaysians
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 24 — Income and wages must remain a priority in the planning of Budget 2027, alongside efforts to strengthen the capabilities of local companies in high-growth, high-value (HGHV) industries. Akmal said the allocation to Penang for the development of the National Automation, Testing and Equipment (ATE) Campus in Batu Kawan was also part of the government’s efforts to strengthen local companies’ capabilities, thereby creating better job opportunities and more meaningful wages for Malaysians. Meanwhile, Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state government would provide land in Batu Kawan for the development of the ATE campus.

items.title: Viral clip of foreign hawker's stall being vandalised sparks debate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A viral video showing local men confronting a foreign hawker and kicking down his stall has sparked an intense debate online. In the 35-second clip, several men confront a foreigner preparing betel leaf (paan), demanding that he pack up immediately. The incident drew split reactions online.

items.title: Penang DVS probes case of dog allegedly dragged by motorcycle in Batu Lancang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 24 — The Penang Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) is investigating an incident involving two men who allegedly dragged a dog using a motorcycle in the Batu Lancang area here yesterday. Penang DVS director Dr Saira Banu Mohamed Rejab, when contacted, confirmed that it had received a report regarding the incident. “The Penang DVS is carrying out further investigations into the incident,” she said.

items.title: KTIP becomes first MIP-supported industrial park on the east coast
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MGB Bhd's Kertih Terengganu Industrial Park (KTIP) has officially secured Managed Industrial Park (MIP) support, becoming the first industrial park on Malaysia's East Coast to achieve this status. It elevates KTIP to the highest tier of professionally managed industrial destinations, reinforcing its appeal to discerning investors targeting the East Coast corridor. This validates MGB's rigorous, forward-thinking management framework - centred on world-class infrastructure, business competitiveness, environmental sustainability, and full operational readiness - cementing KTIP's status as a pivotal regional industrial hub.

items.title: Hajiji: Sabah setting high standards to protect carbon credit reputation
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 24 — Sabah will not permit unvetted projects or speculative trading to undermine its emerging carbon market, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Panglima Hajiji Noor said today, insisting that strong regulatory standards are vital to secure long-term investor confidence. Hajiji warned that poorly structured initiatives, exaggerated climate claims, undervalued natural resources, and the exclusion of native indigenous communities would severely damage the credibility of Sabah’s carbon credits on the global stage. Hajiji highlighted that the forthcoming Sabah Climate Change and Carbon Governance Enactment 2025 will provide legal certainty by officially recognising the state government’s ownership of carbon rights, subject to statutory provisions.

items.title: Only RM6.7m recovered from RM2.97b scams, Lim Guan Eng demands urgent action
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 24 — Lim Guan Eng today urged Bank Negara to spearhead a “whole of government” crackdown on digital fraud, cyber theft and scams, warning that billions of ringgit in life savings are at risk. The Bagan MP said elected representatives nationwide have been swamped with complaints from victims, ranging from ordinary Malaysians to professionals such as doctors, engineers and lawyers. He said Bank Negara must lead a coordinated response involving all government departments to curb the surge in crime and protect the life savings of Malaysians.

items.title: Duo identified after dog dragged behind motorcycle
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Veterinary Services Department (DVS) has identified two men caught on video dragging a black dog behind a motorcycle in Batu Lancang, Jelutong. Following the report, Penang DVS director Dr Saira Banu Mohamed Rejab said officers acted immediately to locate the men and rescue the animal. Dr Saira Banu said the department took all animal welfare complaints seriously and urged the public to avoid actions that could cause suffering or harm to animals.

items.title: AirBorneo signed four-year engine maintenance deal with P&W Canada
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: AirBorneo Airways Sdn Bhd has signed a four-year engine maintenance deal with Pratt & Whitney Canada for its ATR 72-500 fleet through 2030. AirBorneo's current fleet consists of eight ATR 72-500 turboprop aircraft powered by PW127M engines. In February this year during the Singapore Airshow 2026 event, AirBorneo announced the acquisition of eight new ATR 600-series aircraft from turboprop manufacturer, ATR.

items.title: Wawasan questions RoS' timing in suspending PN ahead of Melaka polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) has questioned the timing of the Registrar of Societies' (RoS) decision to suspend Perikatan Nasional (PN), as the Melaka election looms. In a statement today, Wawasan said it had been informed of two notices issued by RoS against PN, dated Sept 22 and 23. Wawasan said it would continue working closely with other PN component parties to ensure preparations for the Melaka election proceeded as planned.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB coy over coerced signing allegation, claims ‘overtaken by events’
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 24 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim dodged questions today regarding his police report over claims he was coerced into signing a proclamation on the position of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, claiming the matter has been “overtaken by events”. “Oh, that was a long time ago, overtaken by events. He subsequently lodged a formal police report on September 8 to trigger an official investigation into the alleged coercion.

items.title: Schneider to launch €1.2 billion takeover bid for smart device firm Shelly
items.summary: FRANCE: France's Schneider Electric said on Thursday it intended to launch a voluntary public takeover offer for Bulgarian smart-home device maker Shelly Group for €70 per share. The all-cash offer values Shelly at about €1.2 billion (US$1.4 billion) and is expected to close by the first quarter of 2027, Schneider said in a statement. The offer price represents a 27 per cent premium to Shelly's unaffected reference price as of July 28, and is 22 per cent above its current reference price.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB rejects Anwar’s ‘rude, uncivilised’ claim, says exco acted within role
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 24 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today rejected Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s description of his and the state executive council’s actions as “rude” and “uncivilised”, saying they had not made any decision to remove or appoint the Yang di-Pertuan Besar. Ismail, who is also the Juasseh assemblyman, said the state executive council had instead discussed the state administration’s position on a proclamation presented as the decision of the four Undangs. “The state executive council discussed the state administration’s position on the proclamation presented as the decision of the four Undangs,” he said.

items.title: Body found floating in pond off Jalan Pontian-Skudai
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: An unidentified man's body was found floating near the bank of a pond along Jalan Pontian-Skudai here last night. The operation to retrieve the body was led by commander Inggai Bakau. He said the body was found floating near the pond bank and no identification documents were found on the victim.

items.title: Pensioner who endured seven years of golf balls hitting his home finally wins RM100,000 from Jitra resort
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — A 61-year-old government pensioner has been awarded RM100,000 in damages after enduring nearly seven years of stray golf balls pelting his bungalow in Bandar Darulaman, Jitra. At the Alor Setar High Court, Judicial Commissioner Aimi Zaini Azhar ruled that golf course operator BDB Darulaman Golf & Resort Bhd and landowner BDB Land Sdn Bhd are jointly and severally liable for private nuisance, FMT reported. The court gave the defendants 60 days to heighten and extend safety netting near Hole 7, review tee markers and the line of play, install warning signs, and implement all measures necessary to stop golf balls from entering the property.

items.title: China's fuel inventories hit over decade lows, raising concerns over comeback of export curbs
items.summary: BEIJING: China's gasoline and diesel inventories have fallen to their lowest levels in more than a decade as exports surge and domestic demand recovers seasonally, according to GL Consulting. Low stock levels appear to have raised Beijing's concerns, increasing the prospect of tighter export controls in October, according to Rystad Energy. GL Consulting said it expects exports to fall in October as state refiners prioritise domestic energy security.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB says exco barred from Wisma Negeri, urges review of directive
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 24 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today said state executive councillors (exco) had been barred from entering their offices at Wisma Negeri and urged the relevant authorities to immediately review the directive. Ismail, who is also the Juasseh assemblyman, said he had been informed that the exco members were not only prohibited from entering their respective offices, but were also prevented from carrying out their duties. Ismail said the directive was conveyed to the exco members verbally rather than in writing.

items.title: Malaysia reaffirmed as member of Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group
items.summary: NEW YORK: Malaysia has been reaffirmed as a member of the Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group (CMAG), the body tasked with upholding Commonwealth values and principles. "In this regard, Malaysia continues to be entrusted as a member of the Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group to defend Commonwealth values and principles. The statement added that Mohamad and Botchwey also discussed preparations for the 28th Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM).

items.title: Westports puts sustainability into new facility: Deputy CEO
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Westports Holdings Bhd ensures it incorporates sustainability elements into the development of its new facility which involves stages of detailed study and assessment. Therefore, the company has been very thorough in adopting green aspects into the new facility. Linda said the company conducted a study in 2023 to analyse how much electricity is needed for the new facility.

items.title: Woman reported missing in Kuala Terengganu
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: A 23-year-old woman has been reported missing after leaving her home in Jalan Masjid Bukit Kandis, Kuala Nerus. Kuala Terengganu district police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said police were looking for Nur Bahiyah Ahmad Shukri. Azli said police received a report on the woman's disappearance from her father at the Gong Badak police station on Sept 13.

items.title: [UPDATED] State secretary, legal adviser's positions must be resolved through due process - Negri Sembilan MB
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Any issue concerning the positions of the Negri Sembilan state secretary and state legal adviser should be resolved through the appropriate legal and administrative processes. "The state constitution provides specific mechanisms concerning the appointment of key positions in the state administration. He said the state government respected the federal government, the Attorney-General's Chambers and all institutions established under the Federal Constitution.

items.title: H&M's operating profit grows more than expected in third quarter
items.summary: STOCKHOLM: Swedish fashion retailer H&M on Thursday reported a bigger than expected rise in June-August operating profit, as chief executive officer (CEO) Daniel Erver said his push to control costs and make sourcing more efficient was bearing fruit. H&M meanwhile said it expected sales in September to rise by one per cent measured in local currencies. Gross profit margin widened to 54.0 per cent in the third quarter, from 52.9 per cent last year, which included positive one-off effects from tariffs, H&M said.

items.title: Batu Gajah council empowers community to tackle roaming livestock blamed for road accidents
items.summary: MDBG secretary Muazatul Adawiyah Muhammad said the initiative allowed appointed community agents to act under the Local Government Act 1976 (Act 171) and the MDBG Licensing of Livestock and Stray Animals By-Laws 2012. The initiative involves 16 representatives from the mukims of Tronoh, Lahat, Tanjung Tualang, Sungai Raya and Sungai Terap, who were appointed as MDBG Community Agents for Stray Animal Management. Muazatul said their appointments would be for one year, from October 1 this year until September 30, 2027, in line with the JPKK appointment period.

items.title: Malaysia-China ties built on trust, friendship, not just diplomacy, says Anwar
items.summary: HANGZHOU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has described Malaysia-China ties as having grown beyond ordinary diplomatic relations into a friendship built on trust and confidence. "This relationship goes beyond ordinary diplomatic ties. We need partners who value friendship," he said.

items.title: Australia's Firmus expects US$77mil first-half loss as it plans US$5bil IPO, sources say
items.summary: SYDNEY: Australian data centre operator Firmus expects to lose US$77 million in the current half, according to two people familiar with a draft prospectus, as the firm prepares for a US$5 billion initial public offering (IPO) to fund growth. The IPO would be the second largest ever in Australia, ranked behind Telstra's US$10 billion listing in 1997, according to Dealogic data. Firmus could be valued at up to US$60 billion after the IPO, according to local media reports.

items.title: Digital assets enter institutional era after speculation, infrastructure: Luno chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The global digital asset industry has entered an era of institutionalisation, with tokenisation and stablecoins emerging as key drivers of its next phase, said cryptocurrency platform Luno. Its chief executive officer James Lanigan said the digital asset industry had broadly moved through three eras: speculation, infrastructure and institutionalisation. Lanigan said the industry then entered the infrastructure era from 2018 to 2022, when regulation, custody and institutional infrastructure developed.

items.title: SoftBank raising US$11.1bil in world's biggest high-yield corporate bond sale
items.summary: TOKYO: Tech investor SoftBank Group is issuing US$11.1 billion in dollar- and euro-denominated bonds, set to be the largest high-yield corporate bond sale globally on record as it seeks to fund its mammoth bet on OpenAI. It is also acquiring ABB's robotics business for US$5.4 billion and DigitalBridge for US$3.1 billion. SoftBank is issuing dollar-denominated senior notes of US$1 billion at a 3-1/2-year term, US$4.5 billion at 5-1/2 years and US$4.5 billion at 7-1/2 years, a filing showed.

items.title: Cheras landslide displaces 80 residents; families wait on safety verdict before returning home
items.summary: Kajang Municipal Council (MPKj) Councillor for Zone 6 Tan Kah Hoe said observations and assessments by the relevant agencies, which began yesterday, continued today, with the full technical report expected to be ready within the next few days. The agencies involved include the Public Works Department (JKR), Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS), Minerals and Geoscience Department (JMG) and MPKj. “Block D remains without water supply, while restoring the supply to Block C is taking a little longer as the relevant authorities are identifying the route of the affected pipeline,” he said.

items.title: ‘Many flowers make spring’: Anwar affirms Malaysia open to China’s digital investment
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Malaysia will continue to be open to China’s investment in digital technology as well as cooperation, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Speaking at the 5th Global Digital Trade Expo (GDTE) opening ceremony here Thursday, Anwar credited the Chinese government’s willingness to showcase and share technologies through various platforms. This applies well to the digital economy and (this is) why we will continue to open our economy to benefit digital investments and partnerships.

items.title: EC says 17 new Sarawak seats unlikely ready for next state election
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 24 — The 17 proposed new Sarawak state seats are unlikely to be in place for the next state election, Election Commission (EC) chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said. He said the review of the electoral boundaries for the seats would take longer than February 2027, when the term of the Sarawak government expires. In July, the Sarawak Legislative Assembly passed the State Legislative Assembly (Composition of Members) Bill 2025 to add 17 new seats, bringing the total number of seats from 82 to 99.

items.title: ‘Govern AI or it will govern us,’ Anwar warns in China
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called for an ethics-driven approach to artificial intelligence (AI) and a more open, rules-based digital trade regime to ensure developing nations share in the gains of technological progress. Speaking at the opening ceremony of the 5th Global Digital Trade Expo here, he acknowledged China’s advancement in visualisation and AI as well as its role in sharing technological advancements with the Global South. “The principle remains, either we govern artificial intelligence or artificial intelligence will govern us,” he said, while calling for an ethics-based framework to ensure that innovation and technological advancement remain firmly in the service of humanity He said this was a fundamental issue that touched on the recurring problem of the digital divide, particularly as nations pursued rapid technological advancement amid persistent socio-economic inequalities.

items.title: Home minister: Police probing Negeri Sembilan royal dispute from ‘every angle’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — Police are investigating the escalating royal dispute in Negeri Sembilan from all angles following multiple police reports lodged on the matter, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said. Saifuddin said that while operational details remain confidential, security forces are strictly focused on preserving public order, averting street confrontations, and safeguarding the public, NST reported. “The police have taken preventive security measures to ensure no gatherings could lead to confrontations.

items.title: Former Tabung Haji COO Adi Azuan charged with receiving RM302,000 in house renovations
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 24 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chief operating officer Datuk Adi Azuan Abdul Ghani pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to three counts of graft involving over RM302,000 in home renovation works. Adi Azuan, 56, claimed trial to all charges after they were read out before Sessions Court Judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud, The Star reported. Deputy Public Prosecutor Muaz Ahmad Khairuddin informed the court that the offences were non-bailable, but proposed bail at RM70,000 with one surety should the court exercise its discretion to grant temporary release.

items.title: JPJ denies fake news on Rohingya driving licences, files MCMC report
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 24 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) today denied a statement published on the ‘Along Auto Parts’ Facebook account, titled “JPJ Proposes Allowing Rohingyas to Obtain Driving Licenses?” “JPJ takes a serious view of any party producing, modifying, or disseminating content that uses the department’s name, identity, or image in a way that could mislead the public and undermine JPJ’s credibility,” the department said in a Facebook post today. The public is advised not to spread information of unverified authenticity and to always refer to official JPJ channels for accurate and verified information.

items.title: AGC appeals High Court acquittal of teen in Bandar Utama schoolmate murder case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) has filed an appeal against a High Court decision that acquitted and discharged a 15-year-old boy of murdering a schoolmate at a secondary school in Petaling Jaya last year. In a statement today, the AGC confirmed that it filed a Notice of Appeal at the Court of Appeal on September 22, seeking to overturn the Shah Alam High Court’s September 14 ruling that freed the teenager of the murder charge under Section 302 of the Penal Code. During the trial, the defence invoked Section 84 of the Penal Code, successfully entering the "unsoundness of mind" defence.

items.title: Azalina: Anti‑Bullying Tribunal resolves five cases with awards, 55 complaints lodged since launch
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The Anti-Bullying Tribunal (TAB) has received 55 complaints, with five cases decided through awards as of Tuesday, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. She said the awards included apologies to victims, participation in a counselling programme and RM2,000 in compensation in one case. Azalina said that, beyond the legal framework, efforts to address bullying also depended on society’s willingness to speak up and take action.

items.title: Woman killed, husband and four children injured in Tanah Merah head‑on collision
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 24 — A woman was killed while her husband and four children were injured in an accident involving their Perodua Alza and a Toyota Hilux at Jalan Rantau Panjang-Panglima Bayu, Tanah Merah, yesterday. Tanah Merah district police chief Supt Mohd Haki Hasbullah said Tengku Ziarulwida Tuan Zainudin, 39, who was a passenger in the Perodua Alza, was killed on the spot in the 3pm incident. He said preliminary investigations showed that the Perodua Alza, driven by Tengku Ziarulwida’s husband, Mohd Saifulzawawi Ghani, 39, collided head-on with the Toyota Hilux.

items.title: Woman found dead in Kuala Kangsar home, police arrest two suspects believed to be relatives
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 24 — A woman was found dead in a pool of blood in the living room of a house in Kampung Cheh Kati, Kuala Kangsar yesterday. Kuala Kangsar police chief ACP Heisham Harun said a report was lodged at 2.38pm after the victim’s family found her lying face down and unconscious inside the house. He said police subsequently arrested two men believed to be related to the victim and suspected to be linked to the case.

items.title: Private hospitals urge government to boost MMC and healthcare watchdog in Budget 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — The Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM) has urged the government to increase federal funding for the Malaysian Medical Council (MMC), warning that persistent underinvestment in the medical regulator threatens to weaken oversight and undermine public trust in the healthcare system. In a press statement today, APHM president Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh said budgetary allocations must be enhanced for the MMC, the statutory body responsible for regulating medical practitioners and upholding professional ethics, alongside the Malaysia Healthcare Travel Council (MHTC). “Sustained underinvestment in these institutions risks weakening oversight, compromising quality assurance processes, and eroding the standards that patients and the public depend on,” the statement said.

items.title: PM Anwar says Malaysia manages disputes with neighbours through dialogue, not distrust
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia manages disagreements with all neighbouring nations through continuous diplomatic engagement and constructive dialogue, rather than conflict or distrust. In a wide-ranging address highlighting the deep cultural and diplomatic ties between Malaysia and China, Anwar shared personal anecdotes of mutual respect and philosophical kinship with Chinese leadership. We are close to China because China is our neighbour.
